subject: Recap: Tool-calling integration patterns (SDK / auth / routing / structured output)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@finapps.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finapps.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Tool-calling integration patterns (SDK / auth / routing / structured output)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for joining the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on integration approach for the FinApps use cases you described (invoice extraction + automated GL mapping + vendor lookup enrichment).

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary flows: 1) user uploads invoice -> extraction model returns structured fields; 2) enrichment layer calls vendor lookup + historical payments; 3) reranker/embeddings used for fuzzy vendor match and GL mapping suggestions.
- Constraints: low-latency UX (sub-500ms target on 90th pct for suggestion path), PCI-PII controls (some fields redaction), and on-prem availability for EU customers later in the roadmap.

Recommended integration pattern (high level):
1) SDK setup & auth
   - Use Redwood SDK server-side for synchronous tool calls. Prefer API-key for server-to-server. For customer-facing clients use short-lived tokens via your auth backend (we can provide token minting endpoints).
2) Routing & model selection
   - Route high-recall extraction to an accuracy-optimized model variant; route suggestion/rerank to a low-latency tuned variant. Use the model routing header in the SDK config to pin versions for testing.
3) Structured output & tool/function calling
   - Define explicit tool schemas for: vendor_lookup, payment_history_query, gl_map_suggester. Each tool returns a typed JSON schema we can validate server-side. Use Redwood's function-calling/structured-output feature so responses are deterministic and easier to reconcile with downstream systems.
4) Embeddings & reranker
   - Store canonical vendor records as embeddings in your vector DB. Use a two-stage approach: ANN nearest-neighbors followed by a reranker using model scoring to produce final match score. Keep the reranker as a separate tool call to allow parallelization and timeouts.
5) Parallel tools & error handling
   - Run non-dependent enrichment calls (vendor_lookup, payment_history_query) in parallel with timeouts (recommend 250ms conservative). If a call fails, fall back to a degraded UX with best-effort suggestions and surface the failure reason in logs/tracing.

Next steps / asks:
- Rafael / Dev: can you prepare a short architecture sketch (sequence diagram + sample tool schemas) and a small code sample showing SDK usage for function calling?
- Alex / Priya: confirm whether FinApps will host the vendor embeddings in your vector DB or if you prefer Redwood-managed vectors. This affects routing and data residency.
- I'll attach a short proposal and a sample code package — Rafael will follow up with detailed tool definitions.

Attachments: redwood-tool-calling-proposal.pdf, finapps-auth-routing-sample-code.zip

Thanks — happy to sync again if you want a walkthrough of the sample code.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Alex / Priya —

Quick answers and a sample schema + integration notes below. Happy to do 30m tomorrow — I have availability 09:00-11:00 PT.

1) PII & data residency
- For your vendor_lookup and reranker paths we support two options: a) Redwood-managed vectors (hosted in the Redwood tenancy) or b) customer-managed vectors (hosted in your VPC/DB). For strict PII controls choose b) — all embeddings and index queries remain in your network.
- We also support field-level redaction in the pipeline: you can configure extraction to redact PAN/SSN and return only tokenized/masked fields to downstream tools.

2) Timeout & graceful degradation
- Pattern: optimistic parallel calls. Kick off vendor_lookup and payment_history_query in parallel with a 250–400ms deadline. Meanwhile run embeddings ANN + reranker as a fallback path. If vendor_lookup returns after the UI timeout, you can patch suggestions (e.g., update row) — but initial response should not block.
- If enrichment fails, surface a confidence drop and log enrichment failure IDs for later reconciliation. We recommend surfacing source and reason in the UI for troubleshooting (e.g., "vendor lookup timed out — suggestions from fuzzy match shown").

3) Sample tool schema (JSON Schema-like). This is a single-line example you can paste into your mocks:
- vendor_lookup(tool input) -> returns vendor record or not_found

Input schema:
{
  "tool": "vendor_lookup",
  "input": {
    "query": "string",            // free-text vendor name or hashed identifier
    "normalized_fields": {         // optional structured fields
      "tax_id_hash": "string",
      "address_tokens": "string"
    },
    "max_results": "integer"
  }
}

Output schema:
{
  "tool": "vendor_lookup",
  "output": {
    "status": "found|not_found|partial",
    "results": [
      {
        "vendor_id": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "match_score": "number",
        "address": "string",
        "confidence_reason": "string"
      }
    ],
    "trace_id": "string"
  }
}

4) SDK usage pattern (pseudocode, server-side Node):
- Initialize the Redwood SDK with an API key stored in your secrets manager.
- Submit a conversation request with function_call definitions for vendor_lookup + payment_history_query + gl_map_suggester.
- Kick off parallel fetches for embeddings-based ANN and the vendor_lookup tool. Use Promise.race / timeout wrappers for vendor_lookup. Merge results based on timestamps and confidence.

Example (sketch):
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const response = await client.generate({
  model: 'redwood-serve-XL',
  input: userPrompt,
  tools: [vendorLookupDef, paymentHistoryDef, glMapDef],
  maxTokens: 200
});

if (response.tool_calls) {
  // validate tool outputs against the schema, then apply business logic
}

5) Next steps I can action by EOD:

- Book 30m tomorrow at 09:30 PT if that works for the FinApps engineering team.

I'll attach the snippets to this thread. Let me know the preferred slot.
